findings.citation_text:
4-301.14 Ventilation Hood Systems, Adequacy. The piece of steaming equipment that is in the back room puts out enough steam that is appears the ceiling tiles overhead are either experiencing condensation drips resulting is peeled ceiling tile surface and possible mold growth. Either way, the steam should be contained to avoid damage to ceiling and walls. The immediate solution was suggested to have the ceiling tiles replaced. findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- The facility is observed to be in a poor state of cleanliness and is continuing to worsen - many of the violations present during today’s inspection are REPEAT violations. There does not seem to be a cleaning schedule in place that is being followed. Floors, walls, drains, and equipment are observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. There are a number of cleaning repeat violations that have not been corrected since previous inspections. Attention to cleaning is needed in the facility. The poor state of cleanliness has caused soil and molds to accumulate throughout food storage and preparation locations and this poses a threat of contamination to food. A follow-up is scheduled for 11/10/2025 to ensure that cleaning is being done, the facility is improving in cleanliness, and that a regular cleaning schedule has been implemented and is being FOLLOWED.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(8) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (C) Responding correctly to the inspector's questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include: (8) Describing the relationship between the prevention of foodborne illness and the management and control of the following: (a) Cross contamination, (b) Hand contact with READY-TO-EAT FOODS, (c) Handwashing, and (d) Maintaining the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT in a clean condition and in good repair.

750-830c A thermometer ±3°F shall be provided to check the temperature of  the water in each tank of the dish machine and the temperature of  the final rinse water as it enters the manifold.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
The left microwave on the cook line had food splatter on the top inside part.  Also, the soda gun holster has mold build up. Wash and sanitize the items.
750-800d The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The drain pipes under the prep cooler had mold build up.  Clean the pipes.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
The right faucet at the 3 compartment sink has a constant drip.  Also, the dish machine pipes leak when the final rinse starts.  Repair leaks.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
findings.comment:
Two dumpsters had their lids open.  Keep dumpster lids closed at all times.
750-1130a Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
The following floors are soiled: A) floor drain by steam cooker (corrected) and bar area (REPEAT) had standing water, B) floor in walk in freezer (REPEAT), C) floor under equipment in bar (REPEAT), D) floor under ice machine (REPEAT). 750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.
(REPEAT) The floor tile and grout in the dish area is damaged.  Fix the tile and grout. Also, a large pipe in the bar area is open and does not have a grate cover.  Install grate.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  **SEE PAGE 2 GENERAL COMMENTS**

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
The walls, door, and ceiling of the walk in freezer have ice build up.  Clean the areas.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
A dipper well with utensils stored in it at the cold line was not running.  Keep dipper well running.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: The following items had damaged caulk: A) the men's urinal and B) the handsink by the wire shelving.  Recaulk the items.  (REPEAT) Also, the foam sealant at the soda carbonation lines was not cut and sealed/painted to allow for proper cleaning.  Cut the foam flat and paint/seal it. 750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: Mold build up was seen in the ice machine.  Wash and sanitize the ice machine. 750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.comment:

750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: The following floors were soiled: A) pooled liquid under soda carbonation, B) debris in the walk in freezer, C) food debris under ice machine, D) floor drains at bar had pooling water due to sludge build up, and E) under equipment in the bar area. 750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Mop heads were being stored in the mop sink. Invert mop heads to facilitate quick drying.
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: .130) Spice containers near the cook line did not have proper labeling.  Properly label all containers.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment: .120) Meatballs located in hot holding were at a temperature of 118  degrees F after the corporate time control of 3 hours.  Make sure all hot foods maintain a temperature of 135 degrees F or remove the food items within the time control limits.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: .120) The following items were not covered in the walk-in cooler:  cooked chicken, wraps and cut celery.  Properly cover all food items when being stored.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment: .160) The following food items had the handles of the utensils touching the ready to eat food: rice at the cook line and chili in the reach in cooler.  All utensils should be stored in a fashion that allows the handles to stick out of the food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment: .280) The dipper well was not running during the time of inspection.  Also, utensils on the hot line were not labeled properly.  Keep the dipper well running and utensils properly labeled.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: .530)  An employee's drink was seen near the cook line.  Employees should only eat or drink in specially designated areas.
